title: Configuring Vim
summary: Chapter 7 presents three mechanisms for applying Vim settings in context: autocommands (with the {event} {pattern} {cmd} form, kept in an augroup with an autocmd! teardown), the vim-editorconfig plugin for .editorconfig files, and Projectionist by Tim Pope for per-project buffer-local configuration. Worked demos move from BufReadPost/BufNewFile/FileType events and :autocmd inspection, through EditorConfig property mapping with its root and precedence rules, to overriding g:ale_linters with b:ale_linters and querying .projections.json files, where the projection nearest the buffer wins. The tip closes by weighing local vimrc files enabled by the 'exrc' option against the restrictions imposed by the 'secure' option. The supplied 5330-6882 range runs past the chapter's end at line 6407 into Appendix 1 and the book's back matter.

concepts.name: BufNewFile event for buffers with no file on disk yet
concepts.evidence: You can use another one of Vim’s events to handle this case: BufNewFile (:h BufNewFile).

concepts.name: FileType event matches the pattern against the filetype
concepts.evidence: Here, the {pattern} is matched against the filetype.

concepts.name: User event as a plugin-defined custom event
concepts.evidence: Plugins can use this mechanism to create their own events.

concepts.name: EditorConfig (.editorconfig) as an editor-agnostic standard
concepts.evidence: The .editorconfig file has become a de-facto standard for specifying settings, scoped by filetype and directory.

concepts.name: EditorConfig precedence: closest config file applied last
concepts.evidence: The closest .editorconfig file is applied last, so any settings specified there will override the settings from above.

concepts.name: Buffer-local b: variables override global g: variables
concepts.evidence: That’s because ALE gives higher precedence to the buffer-local b:ale_linters variable than the global g:ale_linters equivalent.

concepts.name: Projections (.projections.json) scoped to a project directory
concepts.evidence: By placing a .projections.json file in the root directory of your project, you can make Projectionist apply customizations that only affect the files contained in that directory.

concepts.name: Projectionist specificity: nearest projection config wins
concepts.evidence: The proximity between the current buffer and the Projections config file determines the order of the results.

concepts.name: Generalized projection keys decoupled from plugins and options
concepts.evidence: When defining projections, I prefer to use keys that are abstract, rather than choosing keys that are tightly coupled to Vim’s options or to a particular plugin.

concepts.name: Local vimrc file enabled by the 'exrc' option
concepts.evidence: Using this feature, you could create a local vimrc file that customizes Vim’s behavior for a particular project.
